newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Six Turkish navy vessels arrive in north Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Six Turkish navy vessels arrive in north Cyprus.

text.p: Six Turkish navy vessels arrived in the breakaway northern Cypriot state on Friday for anniversary celebrations of Turkey's 1974 invasion of Cyprus, witnesses said.
Two frigates, two gunboats and two submarines docked at Kyrenia harbour in the north of the Mediterranean island for a three-day visit.
The arrival of the vessels sparked anger in the Greek Cypriot-led south, which is internationally recognised as the only legitimate government of the divided island.

"We condemn the arrival of these vessels. They constitute a provocation of great proportions, especially during this period where a solution to the Cyprus problem is being sought," said government spokesman Manolis Christofides.
Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders held talks in the United States last week aimed at resolving the problems of the island's division.
Turkey invaded the northern third of the island on July 20, 1974, in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military then ruling Greece.
Cyprus has since been divided into Greek and Turkish Cypriot sections.
Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit, who ordered the invasion and is still regarded as a hawk on the Cyprus issue, is expected to attend the celebrations on Sunday.
Turkey maintains around 30,000 troops in the north.
